ce_bugs.text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — updateEvent`'s fallback branch computes `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` but this code path only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it searches the array for an entry whose externalId equals a falsy value — effectively always `undefined` — silently discarding the previous behavior of falling back to the event's own destination calendar and causing the Google API call to run with `calendarId: undefined`.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:317 — Same broken fallback pattern in `deleteEvent`: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` compares against the falsy `externalCalendarId` that triggered this branch, so it never finds a match and `calendarId` silently falls back to `"primary"`, meaning delete-by-destination-calendar is effectively broken and could delete/attempt-delete against the wrong (primary) calendar.

mrv_findings.text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:884 — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` uses optional chaining on a value set to `null` when eventType/organizer have no destinationCalendar, so all collected team-member destinationCalendars are silently discarded, defeating the collective multi-host booking feature this diff exists to add (confidence 100, severity P0).

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:122-125 — in `updateEvent`, `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it compares every entry's externalId against that same falsy value and always returns undefined, breaking the previous fallback that resolved a calendar id from the event's destinationCalendar (confidence 100, severity P0).

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:132-136 — identical self-referential `.find` bug in `deleteEvent`'s `calendarId` resolution, so deletes with no externalCalendarId lose the fallback and target `undefined`/`"primary"` instead of the correct destination calendar (confidence 100, severity P0).

packages/core/EventManager.ts:118-119 — `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` (no optional chaining) throws a TypeError whenever destinationCalendar is empty/undefined (confidence 90, severity P1).

packages/core/EventManager.ts:209 — `credentialId: result.credentialId ?? undefined` drops the old fallback to `evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId`, and CalendarManager's `updateEvent` never sets `credentialId` on its EventResult, so every updated/rescheduled BookingReference now loses credentialId tracking (confidence 90, severity P1).

packages/core/EventManager.ts:332-359 — `prisma.credential.findUnique` is now called inside a `for` loop over `event.destinationCalendar`, turning a single credential lookup into an N+1 DB round-trip per destination calendar per booking (confidence 90, severity P2).
packages/core/EventManager.ts:436-461 — same N+1 pattern repeated inside the loop over calendar `references` in `updateAllCalendarEvents`/reschedule flow (confidence 90, severity P2).

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:636-646 — `prisma.credential.findUnique` runs inside the for-loop over `bookingCalendarReference`, another N+1 query pattern introduced on the cancel path (confidence 85, severity P2).

packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:119 — `createEvent(event, credentialId: number)` was added to the shared interface but only GoogleCalendarService consumes it; LarkCalendarService, Office365CalendarService and BaseCalendarService (ics) still pick `destinationCalendar[0]` regardless of which credential is invoking them, so non-Google providers will write every collective host's event into the same first calendar (confidence 75, severity P1).

packages/core/EventManager.ts:366-373 — destinationCalendar entries without a credentialId fan out to every matching-type calendarCredential; with multiple same-integration entries now possible in the array (collective bookings), this can create duplicate calendar events per credential per destination (confidence 60, severity P2).

packages/core/EventManager.ts:118-119 — `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is destructured from a possibly-empty/undefined `destinationCalendar` array and then accessed as `.integration` without optional chaining, throwing a TypeError whenever destinationCalendar is empty or undefined (confidence 90, severity P0).

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:72-76 — createEvent still only reads the first ("mainHost") destinationCalendar entry and never loops over the full array, so in a collective/multi-host booking the event is only created on one host's Office365 calendar instead of all destination calendars (confidence 85, severity P1).

packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:127-130 — createEvent (and createAttendees/updateEvent/deleteEvent) use only the first destinationCalendar entry, so Lark never creates/updates/deletes the event across all hosts' destination calendars in a collective event (confidence 85, severity P1).

packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156-166 — the base ICS/CalDAV service filters calendars using only `mainHostDestinationCalendar`, meaning collective events with multiple destinationCalendar entries only ever target the first host's calendar for CalDAV-based providers (confidence 80, severity P1).

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:254-256 — updateEvent's fallback does `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` inside the branch where `externalCalendarId` is already falsy, so the find predicate can never match and selectedCalendar is always undefined instead of resolving the correct per-host calendar (confidence 75, severity P1).

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:315-317 — deleteEvent has the same tautologically-false `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` fallback as updateEvent, so it never picks a destinationCalendar id and always deletes against `defaultCalendarId` instead of the correct host's calendar (confidence 75, severity P1).

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:251-254,528-531 — destinationCalendar for cancellation is built only from the single booking/user destinationCalendar record, never aggregating team/collective hosts' destinationCalendars the way handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1078 does for creation, so cancelling a collective event won't clean up the calendar entries of the additional hosts (confidence 65, severity P1).

packages/core/EventManager.ts (whole diff) — no unit/integration tests were added or updated for the new multi-destinationCalendar array behavior (looping over destinations, credential-fetch-from-DB fallback, empty-array handling), despite substantial new branching logic in createAllCalendarEvents and updateAllCalendarEvents (confidence 90, severity P2).
